### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata`, `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **44** documentable anchor(s).

**26** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **32** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `47f41f015155ef8596da429b9be3318d83fc2872` — the merge of head `c79d8ff7092f590b66370a2015d16f675389579d` into base `f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 47f41f015155ef8596da429b9be3318d83fc2872 && git checkout 47f41f015155ef8596da429b9be3318d83fc2872
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148 c79d8ff7092f590b66370a2015d16f675389579d && git checkout -B drift-repro f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148 && git merge --no-ff c79d8ff7092f590b66370a2015d16f675389579d

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs f2abd4767b32200bcbd866cd34e0b2863f06d148` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

domain:server#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmRb3wUaRcujR7QEm2o

**Both items from the preliminary epic review (6729460160) are fixed at head `054df525`.**

**Item 1: picklist referrer with more than one packaged contributor.**
- `picklistReferrerOf` now returns every packaged `own`/`extend` contributor whose own declaration names that picklist on the field, each package once. It no longer keeps only the last one.
- The new `SchemaRegistry.resolveFieldPicklistOptions` asks R once per referrer. The field is served only when every referrer resolves to the same holder (`sameHolder`). Any other outcome serves no options, so the validator refuses the field's values: one referrer refused or reaching nothing, or two reaching different holders.
- The boot audit already judges each packaged contributor separately (`auditPicklistReferences`). So each referrer whose own resolution refuses is named, with R's sentence and its candidates.
- Under phase 1, a disagreement can only be one referrer resolved and another refused. A package caller never reaches the environment's item, and a picklist name has at most one package holder.
- Pin in `engine-picklist.test.ts`, "two packages writing one field's reference: served no options unless BOTH reach the list (no fold-order pick)". The owner has no dependency on the list's package and the extender, folded last, does. The field is served no options, and the audit names `com.test.pkg`. A CONTROL test has both depending on it and the list is served.
- Ablation (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, last-wins put back): the pin goes red, 1 failed / 31 passed. Restored with blob == HEAD.

**Item 2: the install judge's artifact-wide `declared.has` short-circuit.**
- The artifact-wide set is gone. Each reference short-circuits only on its own manifest's lists (`collectManifestPicklistNames(manifest)`). Everything else is answered by `picklistReferenceVerdict(…, ordered)`.
- `withPendingManifests` now also lists each pending manifest's `picklists` as held by that manifest's package. Before, it overlaid only `getPackage`. So R judges a sibling's list through the referrer's declared closure, the way the served field will once the artifact registers. Extension targets are still judged caller-less.
- Pins in `plugin-picklist-boot-audit.test.ts`, describe "the picklist install door — a sibling in the same artifact (ADR-0150 D3)":
  - A two-package artifact whose app has no dependency on the sibling holding the list is refused. The refusal names `package "com.test.suite.lists"` and nothing registers. This is the N1 arm, marked as pending the ruling.
  - CONTROL: the same artifact with the dependency registers and is served the list.
- Ablation (the artifact-wide set put back): the refusal pin goes red, 1 failed / 10 passed. Restored with blob == HEAD.

**Runs on `054df525`:**
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql typecheck && … test` under the lock: 571 files passed and 11659 tests passed. The same two tests are red as before, both still held: the N1 residual test and the core-boundary ratchet (R2 #31733).
- eslint on `packages/objectql/src` (`--no-inline-config`): exit 0.

Still owed for the final head: merge `main` once R2 #31733 lands, then the gates and the dogfood battery again on that head.

domain:server#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmRb3wUaRcujR7QEm2o

**CI on `62e2f40c`: two red checks, and neither is a new defect.**

- **Build Core** ([job 128913936556](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42540394083/job/128913936556)) fails at `check:lean-entry-closure`. It reports FORBIDDEN `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` in the `@objectstack/objectql/core` closure, and UNLISTED `@objectstack/lint` and `@objectstack/sdui-parser`, which it pulls in. This is the R seam the body already declares (Acceptance notes, "Held red, pending R2"). `package-scoped-resolver.ts` statically imports `packageDependencyClosure` from the root barrel of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, and this PR is the first time `registry.ts` calls it from the core closure. R is not this card's to edit. The root fix is R2 #31733: the resolver core moves to `@objectstack/core` and the closure walk moves to `@objectstack/metadata-core`. This branch merges `main` once R2 lands. It will stay red on `054df525` too, for the same reason.
- **TypeScript Type Check** ([job 128917572711](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42540394052/job/128917572711)): the `typecheck-workspace` lane concluded `cancelled`, not failed. The push of `054df525` superseded that run, and the run on the new head is in progress. Locally, `typecheck` for `@objectstack/objectql` and `@objectstack/metadata` exits 0 on both heads.

domain:server#2 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmRb3wUaRcujR7QEm2o

**Test Core (1/8) on `054df525`** ([job 128918340435](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/actions/runs/42541586593/job/128918340435)): three tests are red in `@objectstack/cli`. I reproduced all three locally (`packages/cli`, `vitest run` on the two files: 3 failed / 12 passed).

- `picklist-references.boot-parity.test.ts`, both cases ("a list a SIBLING package of the same artifact declares: both doors accept it" and "a name no package of the artifact declares: both doors refuse it, at the same field"). The fixture artifact has `com.example.parity.core` naming a list that its sibling `com.example.parity.app` declares, with no declared dependency between them. So the boot refuses it with R's outside-closure sentence. This is the N1 arm, held with the residual test until the maintainer's ruling on #31678.
- `seed-record-values.test.ts` › "judges a picklist-bound field against the options the stack's picklist resolves". **This one is this PR's, and it is not declared yet.** The cli judge registers the stack's picklists package-less, and its objects through `ObjectQL#registerObject` with no package, which defaults to `'__runtime__'`. R treats `'__runtime__'` as a package, so D3 (a) refuses the environment list. This is a narrowing wider than the declared one. I've put it to the epic seat with options, and I'm recommending treating the compatibility default `'__runtime__'` as a package-less referrer. Nothing is pushed until that is ruled.
